title: Google Renames Gemini Again: Full Breakdown of New Feature Functions – Android Police
body:
Google has announced another round of rebranding for its AI‑powered productivity suite, consolidating a bewildering array of feature names under a more streamlined terminology. The move, revealed in a detailed field guide released on Tuesday, replaces the previously introduced “Gems,” “Skills,” “Spark,” and “Scheduled Actions” with new designations that aim to clarify each tool’s purpose within the Gemini ecosystem. The changes arrive as Google seeks to simplify user experience and differentiate its offerings from a crowded market of generative AI assistants.

The first of the renamed components, formerly known as “Gems,” will now be called “Insights.” These are the contextual snippets that Gemini generates in response to user prompts, offering quick facts, summaries, or creative suggestions without launching a full‑blown conversation. By renaming them “Insights,” Google underscores their role as concise, data‑driven takeaways that can be inserted directly into documents, emails, or chat threads, reducing the cognitive load on users who previously had to remember the more abstract “Gems” moniker.

“Skills,” the set of pre‑trained, task‑specific models that could draft code, design graphics, or compose music, have been rebranded as “Specialties.” This shift reflects a broader strategy to present these capabilities as professional‑grade competencies rather than casual add‑ons. Each Specialty can be invoked with a natural‑language trigger, allowing users to say, for example, “Create a marketing flyer” and have Gemini pull from its design Specialty to generate a ready‑to‑use layout. The rename also aligns the feature with Google’s enterprise narrative, positioning Gemini as a versatile assistant for both personal and business workflows.

The “Spark” feature, which previously acted as an idea‑generation engine for brainstorming sessions, will now be known as “Catalyst.” Catalyst is designed to kick‑start creative projects by proposing outlines, story arcs, or product concepts based on minimal user input. Google’s documentation highlights that Catalyst can maintain context across multiple iterations, enabling a more fluid dialogue between the user and the AI. By emphasizing the catalytic nature of the tool, Google hopes to convey that it is not merely a static suggestion box but a dynamic partner that accelerates the creative process.

Finally, “Scheduled Actions,” the automation layer that allowed users to set future tasks for Gemini—such as sending reminders, drafting follow‑up emails, or posting updates at a predetermined time—has been renamed “Timelines.” This new label is intended to make the feature’s temporal aspect more intuitive. Timelines integrates with Google Calendar and Workspace, giving users the ability to queue AI‑driven actions alongside human‑planned events. The change also signals a deeper integration with Google’s broader productivity suite, positioning Gemini as a proactive scheduler rather than a reactive tool.

Industry analysts view the rebranding as a double‑edged sword. On one hand, the clearer nomenclature could reduce friction for new adopters and help Google compete with rivals like Microsoft’s Copilot and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which have benefited from more straightforward feature naming. On the other hand, the frequent renaming may erode brand trust among power users who have already invested time learning the previous terminology. “Consistency is key in building a loyal user base for AI assistants,” notes Maya Patel, a senior analyst at TechInsights. “If Google continues to shuffle names, it risks alienating the very audience that drives enterprise adoption.”

Beyond semantics, the updates hint at a strategic pivot toward tighter integration with Google’s existing ecosystem. By aligning Gemini’s components with familiar concepts—Insights, Specialties, Catalyst, and Timelines—Google is positioning the AI as an embedded layer within Workspace, Android, and Chrome, rather than a standalone chatbot. This could accelerate the rollout of Gemini‑powered features across the company’s product line, from real‑time document editing to automated meeting summaries.

Looking ahead, the success of Google’s rebranding will depend on how effectively the company can translate the new terminology into tangible productivity gains for users. If the renamed features deliver on their promises—providing quick, accurate insights, specialized task execution, creative catalysis, and reliable scheduling—Google may finally achieve the seamless AI experience it has long pursued. As the AI assistant market matures, clarity and consistency will be as crucial as raw capability, and Google’s latest naming overhaul could be the catalyst that steadies its course toward broader adoption.
